title: The Call of Abraham, part 3 of 5: the stars, the promise believed, and the covenant between the pieces
style: Classical oil painting on canvas, visible expressive brushstrokes and palette-knife texture, dramatic chiaroscuro, rich earthy palette of ochre, umber, olive and deep blue. The age of the patriarchs in the ancient Near East, about four thousand years ago: people dressed in simple garments of wool or linen, undyed or dyed in earth colours, tents of black goat hair, tools of wood, stone and bronze, nothing man-made beyond what the scene describes. Cinematic 16:9 landscape composition. No text, no borders, no watermark, no modern objects.

ABRAM.name: Abram
ABRAM.desc: Abram, a tall, strong, upright man who looks about sixty, with warm brown weathered skin, thick wavy dark hair heavily streaked with grey reaching his collar, a full grey-streaked beard, a strong straight nose and steady, thoughtful dark eyes, wearing an ankle-length long-sleeved tunic of undyed cream wool with a brown leather belt and a deep russet-red wool mantle draped over his left shoulder, and simple leather sandals

SARAI.name: Sarai
SARAI.desc: Sarai, a strikingly beautiful, graceful woman who looks about forty-five, with warm brown skin, large dark eyes, high cheekbones and long wavy black hair with a few silver threads, her hair mostly covered by a long indigo-blue wool head shawl that falls over her shoulders, wearing an ankle-length long-sleeved dress of undyed cream wool with a woven belt of red and blue, and simple leather sandals

blocks.SERVANTS: herdsmen and serving women in knee-length tunics and ankle-length dresses of rough wool in undyed cream, brown and grey, the women with plain head shawls
blocks.CANAAN: the hill country of Canaan: rolling limestone hills with grey rock ledges, spring grass, wild flowers, scattered olive trees and thickets of evergreen oak
blocks.CANAANTOWN: a small walled Canaanite town of pale stone and mud brick with flat roofs, crowning a hilltop; no domes, no arches, no columns, no towers with pointed roofs
blocks.CANAANITES: Canaanite townsmen, bearded men with shoulder-length black hair held by headbands, in knee-length wrapped wool kilts and tunics with red and blue woven borders
blocks.OAK: an enormous, ancient oak tree with a massive gnarled trunk and a broad, spreading crown of dark green leaves
blocks.NEGEV: the Negev: a dry southern land of pale stony hills, dusty gullies and sparse grey thorn scrub under a hard blue sky
blocks.CARAVAN: a caravan of laden grey donkeys and a flock of sheep and goats
blocks.UR: the city of Ur: a great walled city of tan mud brick, crowded with flat-roofed houses, standing beside a broad river with reed boats drawn up on its bank and date palms along the water; no domes, no arches, no columns, no statues
blocks.SALEM: a small walled town of pale limestone with flat roofs on a rocky ridge above the valley; no domes, no arches, no columns, no towers with pointed roofs, no temple
blocks.NOHALO: No halo, no rays and no glow around any person
blocks.ELIEZER: Eliezer of Damascus, the steward of Abram's household, a lean, capable man of about forty with light olive-brown skin, short curly black hair, a neatly trimmed black beard and alert eyes, wearing a knee-length tunic of brown-and-cream striped wool with a leather belt and a small leather pouch hanging from it, and leather sandals
blocks.INTENT: inside a tent of black goat-hair cloth at night, with wooden poles, woven rugs on the ground, a sleeping mat and one small clay oil lamp burning with a single flame
blocks.STARS: an immense, clear night sky crowded from edge to edge with thousands upon thousands of sharp bright stars and the pale band of the Milky Way; no moon, no clouds, no shooting stars, no comets
blocks.NOGORE: No blood, no wounds, no cut flesh and no bones are shown
blocks.FIREPOT: a smoking firepot: a round-bellied clay pot about knee high with a wide open mouth, glowing red-orange from the fire inside it and pouring thick grey smoke from its mouth
blocks.TORCH: a flaming torch: a short bundle of dry sticks bound with cord, burning at its top with a tall bright yellow-orange flame
blocks.NOCARRY: No person, no hand, no arm and no figure of any kind carries, holds or stands near the firepot and the torch: the two of them hang upright in the air by themselves a little above the ground, side by side
blocks.VISION: Painted as a dim vision seen in sleep: all the people are small dark silhouettes without faces, seen against a smoky amber glow, and the edges of the picture are lost in deep darkness
blocks.NOEGYPT: No pyramids, no sphinx, no obelisks, no statues and no writing anywhere
blocks.DARK: The darkness is only darkness: no shapes, no faces, no eyes, no creatures and no figures in it
blocks.HALVES6: two short facing rows of bulky, rounded dark shapes lying on bare earth, with a clear straight path of bare earth a few paces long between the rows. There are exactly six shapes in all and no more: three in the left row and three in the right row, and in each row one is reddish-brown, one is black and one is white. They are the halves of a heifer, a goat and a ram, each as big as half of the animal's body and lying with its hide upward so that only hide is seen; they are not flat skins. No blood, no cut flesh, no bones and no entrails are visible anywhere

segs.text: After these events, the word of the LORD came to Abram in a vision:
Do not be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, your very great reward.
But Abram replied,
O Lord GOD, what can You give me, since I remain childless, and the heir of my house is Eliezer of Damascus?
Abram continued,
Behold, You have given me no offspring, so a servant in my household will be my heir.
Then the word of the LORD came to Abram, saying,
This one will not be your heir, but one who comes from your own body will be your heir.
And the LORD took him outside and said,
Now look to the heavens and count the stars, if you are able.
Then He told him,
So shall your offspring be.
Abram believed the LORD, and it was credited to him as righteousness.
The LORD also told him,
I am the LORD, who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldeans to give you this land to possess.
But Abram replied,
Lord GOD, how can I know that I will possess it?
And the LORD said to him,
Bring Me a heifer, a goat, and a ram, each three years old, along with a turtledove and a young pigeon.
So Abram brought all these to Him, split each of them down the middle, and laid the halves opposite each other. The birds, however, he did not cut in half.
And the birds of prey descended on the carcasses, but Abram drove them away.
As the sun was setting, Abram fell into a deep sleep, and suddenly great terror and darkness overwhelmed him.
Then the LORD said to Abram,
Know for certain that your descendants will be strangers in a land that is not their own, and they will be enslaved and mistreated four hundred years.
But I will judge the nation they serve as slaves, and afterward they will depart with many possessions.
You, however, will go to your fathers in peace and be buried at a ripe old age.
In the fourth generation your descendants will return here, for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet complete.
When the sun had set and darkness had fallen, behold, a smoking firepot and a flaming torch appeared and passed between the halves of the carcasses.
On that day the LORD made a covenant with Abram, saying,
To your descendants I have given this land—from the river of Egypt to the great River Euphrates—
the land of the Kenites, Kenizzites, Kadmonites,
Hittites, Perizzites, Rephaites,
Amorites, Canaanites, Girgashites, and Jebusites.

stills.prompt: {EMPTY}. After these events: a quiet camp at night in a green valley among the hills, a grove of several enormous ancient oak trees with massive trunks and spreading crowns standing over a few black goat-hair tents, the red embers of one camp fire on the ground, sheep lying asleep in the grass, and a faint glow of lamplight inside the nearest tent. Starry sky above the hills. Wide view.

The word of the LORD came to Abram in a vision: {INTENT}, {ABRAM}, sits alone and awake on the sleeping mat with his head bowed and his hands resting on his knees, as a soft golden light begins to fall on him from above the frame. {ONE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}. Medium view.

Do not be afraid, Abram: {INTENT}, close view of the face of {ABRAM}, lifted toward a warm golden light that falls on him from above the frame, his eyes wide and natural, his lips parted, fear slowly leaving his face. Behind him there is only the dark cloth wall of the tent and one wooden pole: he is indoors, with no sky, no stars, no other tents and no animals in the picture. Head and shoulders only. {ONE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}.

O Lord GOD, what can You give me: {INTENT}, {ABRAM}, kneels looking upward into a golden light that falls from above the frame, both his empty hands held out open before him, palms up, his face earnest and questioning. {ONE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}. Medium view.

Since I remain childless: at dusk, {SARAI}, sits alone on a rug at the open door of {TENT}, her hands lying idle and empty in her lap, looking quietly to one side with a sad, patient face; a wooden spindle and a basket of wool lie beside her. There is no child anywhere in the picture. {ONE}. Medium view.

The heir of my house is Eliezer of Damascus: in morning light at the edge of a camp of black goat-hair tents, {ELIEZER}, stands at the gap of a low sheepfold of piled field stones, counting sheep as they pass through the gap one by one and touching each on the back with a short wooden staff. {ONE}. Medium view.

Behold, You have given me no offspring: close view of the face of {ABRAM}, at night inside a tent, lit by a golden light from above the frame, speaking upward with grief in his eyes and a furrowed brow. Head and shoulders only. {ONE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}.

Then the word of the LORD came to Abram: {INTENT}, seen from behind and to one side, {ABRAM}, kneels with his head lifted as {GLORY}, fills the dark tent and throws his long shadow across the rugs behind him. Exactly one person. Wide view.

One who comes from your own body will be your heir: close view, from the collarbone down to the belt, of a man's two weathered brown hands pressed flat against the chest of his own undyed cream wool tunic, a deep russet-red wool mantle over his left shoulder, warm golden light falling on the hands from above. Only the chest and hands of one man are in the frame, no face.

And the LORD took him outside: at night, {ABRAM}, steps out through the door of {TENT}, holding the tent flap aside with one hand and looking up, following a soft golden light that falls from above onto the ground in front of him. {ONE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}. The light is formless, not a figure. Medium-wide view.

Now look to the heavens: seen from behind, a tall man with grey-streaked dark hair in an ankle-length cream wool tunic and a deep russet-red mantle stands alone and small on an open hillside at night with his head tilted far back, under {STARS}. Dark hills along the horizon. Exactly one man, seen from behind. Very wide view from a low angle.

Count the stars, if you are able: close view of the upturned face of {ABRAM}, in pale starlight, his eyes moving across the sky and his lips parted as he tries to count, one hand lifted with a finger pointing upward; behind him a dark sky full of stars. Head, shoulders and one hand only. {ONE}.

So shall your offspring be: {STARS}, arching over a land of dark rolling hills from horizon to horizon, and far below at the bottom of the picture one tiny man in a cream tunic and a russet-red mantle stands on a bare hilltop with his arms a little open. Exactly one tiny figure. Very wide view.

Abram believed the LORD: close view of the face of {ABRAM}, in starlight, looking upward with calm, steady trust, his eyes bright and wet and a slight smile beginning. Head and shoulders only. {ONE}. {NOHALO}.

And it was credited to him as righteousness: on the open hillside under a sky full of stars, {ABRAM}, kneels with his head bowed and his open hands resting on his knees, while a soft golden light falls on him from above the frame and lies on the grass around him. {ONE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}. {NOHALO}. Medium-wide view.

Who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldeans: seen from behind and high up, {CARAVAN}, with four small figures on foot, travels away from us along a dusty road beside a broad river at sunrise, leaving behind in the foreground corner the walls of {UR}. Exactly four small figures, seen from behind. No camels, no carts. Very wide high view.

{EMPTY}. To give you this land to possess: {CANAAN}, rolling away ridge after ridge to a far horizon in the first golden light of dawn, with mist lying in the valleys. No buildings. Very wide high view.

Lord GOD, how can I know that I will possess it: at dawn on the hillside, {ABRAM}, stands with one hand laid on his chest and the other held out open toward the land behind him, his face lifted, asking earnestly, golden light on his face and the hills of the land beyond him. From the waist up. {ONE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}.

Bring Me a heifer, a goat, and a ram, each three years old: in morning light, exactly three animals stand side by side in a small pen of piled field stones, all three alive and calm. From left to right they are: one young reddish-brown cow without horns; one black long-haired goat; and one white ram with heavy curled horns. Exactly three animals, no others. {NOPEOPLE}. Medium view.

Along with a turtledove and a young pigeon: close view of a man's two weathered brown hands holding a small cage of woven twigs in which exactly two living birds sit side by side: one slim pinkish-brown turtledove with a small patch of black and white stripes on the side of its neck, and one plump grey young pigeon. {HANDS}. The cuffs of cream wool sleeves at the wrists. Exactly two birds.

So Abram brought all these to Him: seen from the side in morning light, {ABRAM}, walks from left to right up a grassy slope toward a level place of bare earth near great oak trees, leading one young reddish-brown cow by a rope, with one black long-haired goat and one white ram walking close behind her, and carrying a small cage of woven twigs in his other hand. The cow has no horns. The ram is a full-grown white ram with big, heavy, curled horns on both sides of its head: it is clearly a ram, not a lamb and not a ewe. {ONE}. Exactly three animals. Wide view.

Split each of them down the middle, and laid the halves opposite each other: in afternoon light on a level place of bare earth near great oak trees, {ABRAM}, stands at the near end of {HALVES6}, bending forward with both hands resting on the nearest shape as he sets it in its place. He holds nothing in his hands. {ONE}. No living animals. Wide view from a little above, looking along the path between the rows.

The birds, however, he did not cut in half: close view of the bare earth path, with one whole turtledove lying still on a flat stone on the left side of the path and one whole grey young pigeon lying still on a flat stone on the right side, facing each other, their feathers smooth and unbroken; a man's weathered hand is just drawing back from the pigeon. Exactly two birds, both whole. {NOGORE}. Only one hand and forearm in the frame, no face.

And the birds of prey descended on the carcasses: seen from the ground looking up in afternoon light, five large dark birds of prey, vultures and kites with broad ragged wings, glide down in a spiral out of a pale sky toward {HALVES6}, in the lower part of the picture. {NOPEOPLE}. Wide view from a low angle.

But Abram drove them away: {ABRAM}, runs along the path between {HALVES6}, swinging his wooden staff high with both hands and shouting, while three great vultures flap heavily up into the air in front of him with beating wings and flying dust. {ONE}. {NOGORE}. Wide view from a little above.

As the sun was setting: {ABRAM}, sits wearily on the ground with his staff across his knees, his head beginning to nod, at the near end of {HALVES6}, while behind him a great red sun sinks half below the dark western hills and long shadows stretch over the bare earth. The ground around is empty open earth and grass. {ONE}. Wide view from a little above.

Abram fell into a deep sleep: close view of {ABRAM}, lying asleep on his side on the bare ground with his head pillowed on his folded arm and his russet-red mantle pulled over his shoulder, his eyes closed, in the last dim red light of dusk. Head, shoulders and one arm only. {ONE}.

And suddenly great terror and darkness overwhelmed him: close view from above of {ABRAM}, lying asleep on the ground with his eyes shut tight, his brow knotted in dread and one hand clenched in the cloth of his mantle, while a deep, heavy blackness closes in on him from every side so that only his face and hand can still be seen. {ONE}. {DARK}.

Your descendants will be strangers in a land that is not their own: a long column of families on foot, men, women and children with bundles, donkeys and flocks, walks down into a wide, flat, foreign land of a river, reeds and palm trees. {VISION}. {NOEGYPT}. Very wide view.

And they will be enslaved and mistreated: rows of bent men and women carry heavy baskets and stacks of mud bricks on their shoulders and backs across a flat brickfield, while three overseers stand over them holding rods upright at their sides. {VISION}. No blow is struck, no one lies on the ground. {NOEGYPT}. Wide view.

Four hundred years: close view of the cracked, clay-caked hands of a very old labourer setting a wet mud brick out of a wooden mould onto the ground at the end of a line of drying bricks that runs away into a dim amber haze, while beside them the small clay-caked hands of a child set down another brick in the same way. Only two pairs of hands and forearms are in the frame, no faces. {NOEGYPT}.

But I will judge the nation they serve as slaves: over a great walled city of mud brick beside a river on a flat plain, a vast, towering storm-dark sky breaks open and {GLORY}, strikes down upon the city walls, and in the foreground three overseers have dropped their rods and cower with their arms over their heads. {VISION}. No fire falls and the city is not burning. {NOEGYPT}. Very wide view.

And afterward they will depart with many possessions: a great multitude of men, women and children walks out of the flat land toward a bright glow ahead of them, upright and free, carrying bundles, jars and rolled cloths on their shoulders and leading laden donkeys, cattle and flocks. {VISION}. No overseers, no rods. {NOEGYPT}. Very wide view from behind.

You, however, will go to your fathers in peace: at the open door of a black goat-hair tent at sunset, a very old man with long white hair and a long white beard sits at rest in profile with his eyes closed and his hands folded over the top of his staff, the warm low sun full on him and oak trees behind. He is seen as a warm dark shape against the sunset, his features soft and unclear. Exactly one person. Medium view.

And be buried at a ripe old age: {EMPTY}. In quiet evening light, the dark mouth of a burial cave opens in a low limestone rock face at the edge of a field, with a large rough stone leaning beside the opening, old trees standing along the edge of the field and tall grass moving before it. No body, no bones. Wide view.

In the fourth generation your descendants will return here: seen from behind, a great crowd of men, women and children with flocks and bundles comes up over the crest of a ridge and looks down into {CANAAN}, bright in morning light below them. {VISION}. Very wide view from behind.

For the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet complete: at dusk, {CANAANTOWN}, its windows and gate red with torchlight, stands under a huge, dark, heavy sky; the shadow of the clouds has covered the lower half of the hill and the town's wall, while the roofs at the top are still in the last pale light. No fire falls, the town is not burning, no ruins. {NOPEOPLE}. Very wide view.

When the sun had set and darkness had fallen: in deep night under a few faint stars, {HALVES6}, barely seen in the dark, and at the near edge the small dark shape of one man lying on the ground wrapped in his mantle. Everything is still and almost black. Exactly one small figure lying down. Wide view from a little above.

Behold, a smoking firepot and a flaming torch appeared: in deep night at the far end of a bare earth path, {FIREPOT}, and beside it {TORCH}. {NOCARRY}. Their fire lights the bare ground under them and the nearest dark hide-covered shapes lying on both sides of the path. {NOPEOPLE}. {NOGORE}. Medium view from a low angle.

And passed between the halves of the carcasses: seen from above and behind in deep night, {FIREPOT}, and beside it {TORCH}, move away from us down the middle of the clear path between {HALVES6}, their firelight glowing orange on the hides on both sides and a long trail of grey smoke hanging in the air behind them. {NOCARRY}. {NOPEOPLE}. Wide view from a little above.

Very close view from ground level in deep night: {FIREPOT}, passes just above the bare earth of a narrow path, with the bright flame of a torch of bound sticks burning beside it, sparks drifting, and on the left and right edges of the picture the dark hide of large shapes lying on the ground glows orange in the firelight. {NOCARRY}. {NOPEOPLE}. {NOGORE}.

On that day the LORD made a covenant with Abram: in deep night, {ABRAM}, kneels on the bare earth with his face lifted and his hands open, lit warm orange from one side by firelight from outside the frame and from above by a soft golden light, a haze of grey smoke hanging in the dark air behind him. {ONE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}. {NOHALO}. Medium view.

{EMPTY}. To your descendants I have given this land: seen from a great height just before sunrise, a whole country of green hills, valleys, a long river valley and a far bright sea lies spread out under a sky where the last stars are fading and a band of gold is growing along the horizon. No buildings. Very wide high view.

{EMPTY}. From the river of Egypt: very close, low view of clear shallow water flowing over sand between low sandy banks with green reeds and a grey-green tamarisk bush at the edge of a pale desert, in bright morning sun. Only the near bank and the water are seen: the far bank and the width of the river are outside the picture. No boats, no buildings.

{EMPTY}. To the great River Euphrates: a very broad, slow, brown-green river sweeps in a wide bend across a flat northern plain between banks of poplar and willow trees and beds of tall reeds, under a huge sky with the sun low. No boats, no bridges, no buildings. Very wide high view.

The land of the Kenites, Kenizzites, Kadmonites: in {NEGEV}, a small camp of black goat-hair tents stands by a well, and in front, a bearded smith in a leather apron kneels at a small clay furnace working a goatskin bellows with one hand, while two herdsmen in rough wool tunics water goats at the well behind him. Exactly three men. Medium-wide view.

Hittites, Perizzites, Rephaites: in bright daylight among {CANAAN}, farmers of an unwalled village of small stone houses with flat roofs thresh grain on a round threshing floor, one man driving two oxen round and round over the sheaves and two women tossing grain in flat baskets, and far behind them on a hilltop stands {CANAANTOWN}. The villagers are {CANAANITES}, and women in long wool dresses with head shawls. Wide view.

Amorites, Canaanites, Girgashites, and Jebusites: in early morning light, {SALEM}, and on the stony road that climbs to its gate a short line of {CANAANITES}, leads three laden donkeys up toward the town. Wide view from across the valley.

Seen from behind at first light, a tall man with grey-streaked dark hair in an ankle-length cream wool tunic and a deep russet-red mantle stands alone on a hilltop of grass and grey rock with a wooden staff in his hand, looking out over an immense land of hills and valleys turning gold in the sunrise. Exactly one man, seen from behind. Very wide view from behind.

card_notes: Every spoken word is Scripture: Genesis 15:1–21, complete.
notes: Text: Genesis 15:1-21 in full, no verses skipped or abridged. Speakers: N narrator, G the voice of God (as in earlier units), A Abram (15:2-3, 15:8, same voice as s02e01a and s02e01b).
Still tags: T = from the text, I = inferred, D = dramatized. Still 'verses' are chapter:verse. No new character sheets in this unit.

Faces: ABRAM and SARAI use the sheets and description text of s01e03b word for word. Eliezer of Damascus (15:2) is seen once (B3) and has a description block only (ELIEZER); his work as steward counting the flock is I. The text does not say that he is the unnamed servant of Genesis 24, and this unit does not decide it.

God is light only (GLORY, or golden light from above the frame); no figure and no face. 'The word of the LORD came to Abram in a vision' (15:1) is pictured as light in his tent at night; 'the LORD took him outside' (15:5) as light that he follows out of the tent, never a figure or a hand.

Order of time follows the text and is not harmonised: stars at night (15:5), then the animals brought and cut by day, birds of prey (15:9-11), then sunset (15:12) and full dark (15:17). Whether the whole chapter is one vision, and how many days it covers, is not resolved. The place is Abram's camp at the Oaks of Mamre (13:18, 14:13), I.
15:1 'your very great reward' follows the BSB main text. 15:2 B2 (Sarai alone at the tent door, no child) is D; she is not named in this chapter. 15:4 D2 shows only a man's hands on his own chest.
15:6: belief and its crediting are pictured only as Abram's face and as light resting on him (no halo, no symbol).
15:7: G1 repeats the departure from Ur as painted in s01e03b (four small figures from behind; 11:31).

15:9-10: heifer, goat and ram are a reddish-brown cow, a black goat and a white ram (colours I; 'three years old' is not picturable). The cutting itself is not shown; the halves lie hide upward in two facing rows with a path between, three in each row, with no blood, flesh or bones visible (block HALVES6: exactly six, three in each row). The whole turtledove and young pigeon lie one on each side of the path (placement I; the text says only that he did not cut them).
15:11: birds of prey are vultures and kites (I). No bird is struck.
15:12: the 'great terror and darkness' is blackness closing in on the sleeping man, with nothing in it (no shapes or creatures).

15:13-16: what God foretells is painted as dim visions of faceless silhouettes (block VISION). The nation is not named in this chapter and none is named or marked in the pictures: a flat river land of reeds, palms and mud brick, with no pyramids, monuments or writing (I; brick-making anticipates Exodus 1:14). No plague of any kind is pictured for 'I will judge' (15:14): only a storm-dark sky and light. 'Four hundred years' (15:13; compare Exodus 12:40) and 'the fourth generation' (15:16) are spoken as written and neither figure is explained or reconciled; M3 (an old labourer's and a child's hands) is D. 15:15: O1 is an unnamed white-haired old man seen against the sunset, not a designed older Abraham; O2 is a burial cave at the edge of a field (I, from Genesis 25:9), with no body shown. 15:16: P2 (cloud shadow halfway up a hill town) is D and shows no particular sin.

15:17: the smoking firepot and flaming torch are a round clay pot of fire and a torch of bound sticks (I) that move by themselves with no one carrying them; only they pass between the pieces (T). What they stand for is not explained on screen. Abram is a small dark shape lying at the edge (Q1): whether he sees this awake or in his deep sleep is not resolved.

15:18: 'the river of Egypt' is disputed (the Nile or its eastern arm, or the Wadi of Egypt): R3 shows only water, sand and reeds close up, with the river's width and far bank out of frame, so neither is chosen. R4 is the Euphrates as a broad river on a northern plain. No map is drawn.

15:19-21: the ten peoples are named by the voice only. S1 (a desert-edge camp with a smith; the Kenites' later link with the south and with metalworking is I), T1 (an unwalled farming village below a hill town) and U1 (a ridge town like the Salem of s02e01b, not labelled) show the land as lived in; they do not say which people is which, and no stature is pictured for the Rephaites because this text gives none. U2 (Abram from behind at sunrise) is D.
Narration is not generated in this unit; shots are laid at assembly.
